gdp_level.source: ONS series YBHA (PN2) · current prices, rolling four-quarter sum, seasonally adjusted.
gdp_level.description: The total value of everything the UK economy produces in a year, at current prices (rolling four-quarter sum of ONS's quarterly GDP series).
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each historical point using that point's OWN contemporaneous GBP/USD rate (monthly resolution, from FRED's DEXUSUK series, which starts 1971-01). Points before 1971 -- this series goes back to 1955 -- have no genuine historical rate available and fall back to the earliest rate DEXUSUK provides (1971-01, £1 = $2.41 approx.), which is disclosed in the page's toggle note. This is a considered approximation for those years, not a precise historical conversion.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to ONS series ABMI (PN2), the chained-volume (inflation-adjusted) measure, on the same rolling four-quarter basis. This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.

gdp_real.source: ONS series ABMI (PN2) · chained volume measure, rolling four-quarter sum, seasonally adjusted.
gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, shown in chained-volume terms -- the same production, valued at constant prices, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.dollar: Same historical-rate matching as GDP (current prices): each point converted at its own contemporaneous GBP/USD rate where available (1971 onward), falling back to the earliest available rate (1971-01) for anything before that.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series -- toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.

gdp_growth.source: ONS series IHYQ (PN2) · chained volume measure, quarter-on-quarter growth rate.
gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous three months, in real (inflation-adjusted) terms.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic -- converting the underlying pounds to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate as published by ONS -- “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.

productivity.source: ONS series LZVB (PRDY) · output per hour worked, index 2023 = 100, seasonally adjusted.
productivity.description: How much the UK produces for each hour worked -- a core measure of how efficiently the economy converts labour into output.
productivity.dollar: This is an index, not a currency figure -- “Make it real” and “Dollarise” don't apply to it.
productivity.real: This is an index, not a currency figure -- “Make it real” and “Dollarise” don't apply to it.

cpi.source: ONS series D7G7 (MM23) · all items.

cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices rose or fell compared with just the previous month -- more volatile than the annual rate, useful for spotting turning points earlier.

boe_rate.source: Bank of England · IUDBEDR, official Bank Rate.
boe_rate.description: The Bank of England's official Bank Rate -- the anchor for most UK mortgage, loan and savings rates. Set by the Monetary Policy Committee.

employment.description: The share of working-age people who are currently in paid work.

gdp_level.source: FRED series GDP · nominal, seasonally adjusted annual rate (BEA).
gdp_level.description: The total value of everything the US economy produces in a year, at current prices, expressed at a seasonally adjusted annual rate.
gdp_level.dollar: US figures are already in US dollars — “Dollarise” is disabled on this page and has no effect.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to FRED series GDPC1, the chained-2017-dollar (inflation-adjusted) measure. This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.

gdp_real.source: FRED series GDPC1 · chained 2017 dollars, seasonally adjusted annual rate (BEA).
gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, shown in chained 2017 dollars — the same production, valued at constant prices, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.dollar: US figures are already in US dollars — “Dollarise” is disabled on this page and has no effect.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series — toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.

gdp_growth.source: FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA · chained 2017 dollars, quarter-on-quarter annualised rate (BEA).
gdp_growth.description: How fast the economy grew or shrank each quarter, in real (inflation-adjusted) terms, expressed at an annualised rate — the standard US convention.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic — “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure, and is disabled on this page anyway since US figures are already in dollars.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate as published by BEA — “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.

productivity.source: FRED series OPHNFB · nonfarm business output per hour, index (BLS).
productivity.description: How much the US produces for each hour worked — a core measure of how efficiently the economy converts labour into output.
productivity.dollar: This is an index, not a currency figure — “Make it real” and “Dollarise” don't apply to it.
productivity.real: This is an index, not a currency figure — “Make it real” and “Dollarise” don't apply to it.

cpi.source: Calculated from FRED series CPIAUCSL · all items, seasonally adjusted (BLS).
cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago. The Federal Reserve targets 2% inflation.

core_cpi.source: Calculated from FRED series CPILFESL · seasonally adjusted (BLS).
core_cpi.description: Inflation excluding volatile food and energy prices — a cleaner read on underlying price pressure, and the measure the Fed watches most closely.

cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices rose or fell compared with just the previous month — more volatile than the annual rate, useful for spotting turning points earlier.

fed_funds.source: FRED series FEDFUNDS · effective rate, monthly average.
fed_funds.description: The Federal Reserve's key interest rate — the anchor for most US mortgage, loan, and savings rates. Set by the FOMC.

unemployment.source: FRED series UNRATE · seasonally adjusted (BLS).
unemployment.description: The share of the labor force who want a job and are actively looking, but can't find one.

employment.description: The share of all people aged 16 and over who are currently in paid work.

participation.description: The share of people either working or actively looking for work.

business_confidence.source: OECD · Business Confidence Indicator (BCICP), amplitude-adjusted, long-term average = 100.
business_confidence.description: How optimistic firms are about the months ahead. 100 is the long-run average; readings above it mean firms expect better-than-average conditions.
business_confidence.dollar: This is an index, not a currency figure — “Dollarise” doesn't apply to it, and is disabled on this page anyway.

fdi.source: World Bank · FDI net inflows, % of GDP, annual (sourced from IMF balance-of-payments data).
fdi.description: Money invested into US businesses from abroad each year (foreign direct investment), as a share of GDP.
fdi.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP — currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

current_account.source: World Bank · % of GDP, annual (IMF balance-of-payments data).
current_account.description: The US's overall balance with the rest of the world — trade in goods and services plus net investment income — as a share of GDP.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP — currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

trade_balance.source: FRED series BOPGSTB · goods and services, seasonally adjusted (BEA/Census).
trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods and services each month. Below zero means the US buys more from abroad than it sells.
trade_balance.dollar: US figures are already in US dollars — “Dollarise” is disabled on this page and has no effect.

exports.source: FRED series BOPTEXP · goods and services, seasonally adjusted (BEA/Census).
exports.description: The value of goods and services the US sells to the rest of the world each month.
exports.dollar: US figures are already in US dollars — “Dollarise” is disabled on this page and has no effect.

imports.source: FRED series BOPTIMP · goods and services, seasonally adjusted (BEA/Census).
imports.description: The value of goods and services the US buys from the rest of the world each month.
imports.dollar: US figures are already in US dollars — “Dollarise” is disabled on this page and has no effect.

trade_intensity.source: Calculated from FRED series BOPTEXP, BOPTIMP and GDP · complete calendar years only.
trade_intensity.description: Total trade (exports plus imports) as a share of GDP — a measure of how open the economy is to international trade.
trade_intensity.dollar: Already a %, and US figures are already in US dollars anyway — “Dollarise” has no effect and is disabled on this page.
trade_intensity.real: Pinned to nominal (current-price) figures deliberately — there's no real-terms exports/imports series to pair with a real GDP denominator. “Make it real” is a no-op for this metric.

debt_gdp.source: FRED series GFDEGDQ188S · total public debt, % of GDP (Treasury/OMB).
debt_gdp.description: Total federal government debt, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP — currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

net_debt.source: FRED series GFDEBTN · total public debt (Treasury).
net_debt.description: The actual stock of US federal government debt in dollars, rather than as a share of GDP.
net_debt.dollar: US figures are already in US dollars — “Dollarise” is disabled on this page and has no effect.

deficit.source: FRED series MTSDS133FMS · Monthly Treasury Statement.
deficit.description: The monthly gap between federal spending and tax receipts. Negative means a deficit; tax-season months (e.g. April) often show surpluses.
deficit.dollar: US figures are already in US dollars — “Dollarise” is disabled on this page and has no effect.
